summary: This work demonstrates a superconducting microwave link between two independently packaged transmon qutrit nodes, achieving arbitrary qutrit-state transfer with 83.68% mean fidelity and 77.12% process fidelity, and generating remote entanglement with negativity 0.730 and tomography-inferred dense-coding capacity 2.273 bits. The protocol uses transition-selective photon-mediated operations ($e0g1$ sideband and $f0g1$ cavity-assisted Raman) to transfer the $|e\rangle$ and $|f\rangle$ amplitudes in distinct temporal modes through a tunable Purcell-filtered interface matched at 7.4347 GHz.
motivation: While superconducting microwave links have enabled deterministic state transfer between qubits, extending this to genuine three-level communication requires mapping the full qutrit Hilbert space onto the traveling field without simultaneously opening all transitions to the continuum. This work tests whether the native three-level structure of transmons can serve as a high-dimensional resource beyond effective qubits.
method: Two transmon qutrits in separate sample boxes are connected by a one-metre cascaded microwave channel. Each node contains an auxiliary transmission resonator and tunable Purcell filter that allow frequency and bandwidth matching between remote interfaces. Two chirped 200 ns sine-envelope pulses implement transition-selective photon-mediated primitives: $e0g1$ couples $|e,0\rangle \leftrightarrow |g,1\rangle$ via flux-parametric sideband, while $f0g1$ couples $|f,0\rangle \leftrightarrow |g,1\rangle$ via cavity-assisted Raman. Full qutrit transfer applies both primitives sequentially; partial transfers generate remote two-qutrit entanglement.
result: Qutrit state transfer exceeds both the classical measure-and-prepare limit (1/2) and the maximum average fidelity 3/4 for transmitting an arbitrary qutrit through a qubit channel. Remote entanglement fidelity 81.21% exceeds the Schmidt-rank-two bound 2/3, negativity 0.730 exceeds the two-qubit maximum 0.5, dense-coding capacity 2.273 bits exceeds the qubit limit 2 bits, and CGLMP parameter $I_3=2.332$ exceeds the local bound 2.
